label: rem:information-bandwidth-remark
title: The information bandwidth as a Bremermann-analog budget
html:
The information bandwidth quantifies the total information transferred across the causal boundary in one Planck step: c_q counts the fibres correlated per tick, and \eta_q the operational entropy carried by each.

At q = q_0, the bandwidth \mathfrak{B} = q\eta_q/(q-1)^2 \approx 82 q-bits per Planck time. This functions as the Bremermann-analog bit budget of the substrate. It dictates the maximum number of distinguishable q-bits that a single Planck step can carry across the light-cone boundary.
